er_v06_c01_b003_01: This price? You didn't try to gouge me after all.
er_v06_c01_b003_02: Hmph. Maybe not everyone down here is a crook.
er_v06_c01_b004_02: I have not sunk so low that a grocer needs to pity me.
er_v06_c01_b004_03: I will take the kindness. Just this once.
er_v06_c01_b005_01: That is all? Even upstairs it is not this expensive.
er_v06_c01_b005_02: I can see that. The goods are from the lower levels. The prices are upper-district.
er_v06_c01_b006_01: What? You don't even have food? And you call this a shop?
er_v06_c01_b006_02: Unbelievable... Fine. I'll look somewhere else.
er_v06_c01_n001_01: Eleanor stands outside the sales window, looks over the shelves through it, then steps up to the counter.
er_v06_c01_n001_02: Oh, so this is what the lower levels call a 'shop'?
er_v06_c01_n001_03: Unbelievable. To frogs who've never left their well, I suppose this passes for acceptable.
er_v06_c01_n001_04: Hey, you over there. Before I go back upstairs, I need something to eat.
er_v06_c01_n001_05: Got anything to eat? Something fresh, and some variety. Don't fob me off with nutrifruit.
er_v06_c01_n001_06: The tags are on them. Look for yourself.
er_v06_c01_n001_08: She points at a packet of snacks. The shopkeeper sets it on the counter; her fingertip stops on the seal. She does not tear it open.
er_v06_c01_n001_09: I never used to have to worry about any of this. They've locked my mother up, claiming she embezzled funds.
er_v06_c01_n001_10: She runs the largest hydroponic farm on the entire station.
er_v06_c01_n001_11: Absurd. Half the station eats because of her!
er_v06_c01_n001_12: It will not be long before they realize what a stupid mistake they have made.
er_v06_c01_n002_01: She doesn't take the bait. Her eyes return to the shelves.
er_v06_c01_n003_02: ...Hmph. Fine. Saves me saying too much and taking it back later.
er_v06_c01_n003_03: This one, and this one. Something that keeps longer, too.
er_v06_c01_n003_04: Three things line up. Her fingertip taps the priciest one, then swaps it for a cheaper packet.
er_v06_c01_n004_01: She counts out coins and sets them on the counter one by one.
er_v06_c01_n004_03: Remember it or don't. I'll be back anyway.
er_v06_c01_n005_02: Remember it or don't. I'll be back anyway.
er_v06_c02_b003_01: Same price you quoted. Fine, I'll take these.
er_v06_c02_b004_02: Do you do this for every customer?
er_v06_c02_b005_01: The same goods cost more here than anywhere else?
er_v06_c02_b005_02: This is my first time living in the lower levels. It doesn't mean I can't do arithmetic!
er_v06_c02_b006_01: Forget it. I'll look around. There must be more than one shop down here.
er_v06_c02_n001_01: She comes up to the sales window with an old cloth over her shoulder.
er_v06_c02_n001_02: I can't believe I'm stuck in a place like this. Why is this happening to me?
er_v06_c02_n001_03: No word from my mother. They won't let me go back up either. I hate it down here. It's so unfair.
er_v06_c02_n001_05: Looks like I'm stuck here for a while.
er_v06_c02_n001_06: A cup, some washing things, and a lamp that actually works.
er_v06_c02_n001_07: I found a decent room across from the ration station. Small, but at least it doesn't stink.
er_v06_c02_n001_08: The shopkeeper sets the chipped cup on the counter. She picks it up and turns it around.
er_v06_c02_n001_09: This cup is chipped. It is not as if I cannot afford a good one.
er_v06_c02_n001_10: ...Never mind. I will take this one. The chip does not affect holding water.
er_v06_c02_n001_11: My roommate says fix the lock first, worry about curtains later.
er_v06_c02_n001_12: She also says the perfume I brought would cover half a month's rent.
er_v06_c02_n001_13: That is perfume custom-made for me by Master Corinna. Hah! Half a month's rent down here!
er_v06_c02_n002_01: She spreads the old cloth on the counter. The shopkeeper hands her a bag; she puts the cup, soap and towel in one by one.
er_v06_c02_n002_02: The two next door argue every night, like they are right beside my bed.
er_v06_c02_n002_03: At least I do not need a radio.
er_v06_c02_n002_04: I can't believe people spend their whole lives in a place like this.
er_v06_c02_n002_06: ...I am not afraid of the dark.
er_v06_c02_n002_07: She picks up the bag, glances back once before leaving, and parts her lips.
er_v06_c03_b003_01: Less than I thought. But the price is fair.
er_v06_c03_b004_02: It'd better be useful. Don't let me come back and find them still here, like they're waiting for pity.
er_v06_c03_b005_01: You know what it's worth. You also know I'm short on money.
er_v06_c03_b005_02: ...Fine. Today you caught me at a bad time.
er_v06_c03_b006_01: Fine, I'll take them. If you won't buy, someone else will.
er_v06_c03_n001_01: She comes early. The shutter has just risen, and she is already outside.
er_v06_c03_n001_03: My funds are running low. They didn't let me bring much with me.
er_v06_c03_n001_04: ...I don't have any other family. Just my mother.
er_v06_c03_n001_05: If I could get back upstairs, I could explain everything.
er_v06_c03_n001_06: Everything could go back to normal, and I wouldn't have to eat Nutrifruit every meal.
er_v06_c03_n001_07: Anyway, I brought some of my own things to sell. Bottled water, toiletries, and perfume.
er_v06_c03_n001_08: Living down here, there is no need to dress as if for a banquet.
er_v06_c03_n001_09: She stands the bottles on the counter one by one and steps back half a pace.
er_v06_c03_n001_10: This perfume has been opened. Twenty percent off.
er_v06_c03_n001_11: A scent blended by Master Corinna... Never mind. You would not understand. Do it your way.
er_v06_c03_n001_12: She tightens the perfume cap and nudges the bottle toward the shopkeeper.
er_v06_c03_n002_02: She draws the pendant from her neckline and holds it face up in her palm.
er_v06_c03_n002_03: My mother gave it to me. Just tell me what it's worth. I haven't decided.
er_v06_c03_n002_05: She tucks the pendant back into her neckline and smooths her collar.
er_v06_c03_n002_06: When I have... decided, I will bring it out again.
er_v06_c03_n003_01: The shopkeeper gently pushes the pendant back and leaves it there.
er_v06_c03_n003_02: You're not even going to name a price?
er_v06_c03_n004_01: He names a price. She listens, then tucks the pendant back under her collar.
er_v06_c03_n004_02: ...The price is fair. But it's not for sale.
er_v06_c03_n005_01: Never mind. ...If I really bring it next time, don't play the big spender.
er_v06_c03_n005_02: I'm going. I'll watch what I spend.
er_v06_c04_b003_01: Hello, shopkeeper. You reported stolen goods?
er_v06_c04_b003_02: I didn't steal it! I have the receipt right here.
er_v06_c04_b003_03: Then why did you report it as stolen?
er_v06_c04_b003_04: Filing a false theft report is a crime. Come along quietly.
er_v06_c04_b003_05: You run a shop, boss. Mind your own counter.
er_v06_c04_b003_06: Someone tampered with my counter. That makes it my business.
er_v06_c04_b004_01: *tells her about the man claiming to be her uncle*
er_v06_c04_b004_02: My uncle? I don't have an uncle.
er_v06_c04_b004_03: I told you. Apart from my mother, I don't have any family.
er_v06_c04_b006_01: The crate was reported stolen, and it's still in my storeroom. Don't touch it.
er_v06_c04_b006_02: A 'gift' that was reported stolen... They wanted me arrested. Just like my mother.
er_v06_c04_b007_01: I didn't take it. He couldn't explain where it came from.
er_v06_c04_b007_03: If anyone else claims to be my family, send him away.
er_v06_c04_b008_01: My mother is already locked up. Isn't that enough for them?
er_v06_c04_b008_03: Before, if someone sent me a crate like that, I wouldn't even check the label. I'd just open it.
er_v06_c04_b008_04: Next time someone brings a box like that, I'll check the label first.
er_v06_c04_b008_05: You warned me. Take this. It's the last thing I brought from home.
er_v06_c04_b009_01: I'll come back when I've sorted out my thoughts.
er_v06_c04_n001_01: A man approaches the sales window carrying a gift box tied with ribbon.
er_v06_c04_n001_02: Hello there. You know Eleanor, don't you? I'm her... uncle.
er_v06_c04_n001_03: We prepared a little gift for her. Only the best from the upper district.
er_v06_c04_n001_04: But I can't find her anywhere.
er_v06_c04_n001_05: I heard she comes here often.
er_v06_c04_n001_06: Next time she visits, could you give this to her?
er_v06_c04_n001_07: Make sure it reaches her hands. Not yours. Hers.
er_v06_c04_n001_08: If anyone asks, you never saw me.
er_v06_c04_n001_09: Oh, and keep Security out of this. It's a family matter.
er_v06_c04_n001_10: He pushes the box a little toward the counter.
er_v06_c04_n002_01: Register? I'm delivering a gift to her, and you want paperwork?
er_v06_c04_n002_02: It's a family matter. Don't ask.
er_v06_c04_n002_03: The man walks away. A farm-supply identification tag is caught under the box, its edges torn.
er_v06_c04_n002_04: Upper-level farm goods reported stolen. Serial logged. Anyone who finds them should report it.
er_v06_c04_n003_01: The box sits under the counter overnight. At the next count, a serial number shows on its base.
er_v06_c04_n003_02: Upper-level farm goods reported stolen. Serial logged. Anyone who finds them should report it.
er_v06_c04_n004_01: Forget it, then. I'll take the box back.
er_v06_c04_n004_02: He pulls the gift box back against his chest and turns to leave.
er_v06_c04_n005_01: The patrol officer arrives quickly, mist still on his cap brim.
er_v06_c04_n005_03: There's a farm serial on the base. The notice says stolen.
er_v06_c04_n005_04: I'll take the goods back. I've logged the serial.
er_v06_c04_n005_05: Has she touched the box? If she has, tell her to come in tomorrow.
er_v06_c04_n005_07: Procedure still requires a word with her.
er_v06_c04_n006_01: The next day she comes later than usual, half-dried mud on her shoes.
er_v06_c04_n006_02: Security knocked on my door this morning.
er_v06_c04_n006_03: Someone left me a box. One that's been reported stolen.
er_v06_c04_n006_04: My uncle? I don't have an uncle.
er_v06_c04_n006_05: I told you. Apart from my mother, I don't have any family.
er_v06_c04_n006_06: They wanted me arrested. Just like my mother.
er_v06_c04_n006_07: She's already locked up in there. Isn't that enough for them?
er_v06_c04_n006_08: She grips the edge of the counter, fingers digging into the seam, back straight.
er_v06_c04_n006_10: There was a serial on the base. The notice said stolen.
er_v06_c04_n006_11: ...You were right to report it. But next time, don't decide for me.
er_v06_c04_n006_13: Before, if someone sent me a crate like that, I wouldn't even check the label. I'd just open it.
er_v06_c04_n006_14: Next time I'll check the label first.
er_v06_c04_n007_01: You warned me. Take this. It's the last thing I brought from home.
er_v06_c04_n008_01: She stops after a few steps, looks back at the counter, then keeps walking.
er_v06_c05_b004_01: ...I understand. You run a shop, not a charity.
er_v06_c05_b004_02: When I have money, I'll buy at full price.
er_v06_c05_b006_01: Don't tell anyone I came here to beg today.
er_v06_c05_b007_01: Don't move! That crate was reported stolen.
er_v06_c05_b007_02: What? It's not mine! I've never seen it before!
er_v06_c05_b007_03: Like mother, like daughter. Come with us.
er_v06_c05_b007_04: Please, someone set me up! Shopkeeper, tell them!
er_v06_c05_b009_01: You were tricked too. ...But next time, ask me first. All right?
er_v06_c05_b010_01: You knew it was reported stolen?
er_v06_c05_b010_03: Then don't act as if getting me out makes it never happen.
er_v06_c05_n001_01: She waits outside the window for a long time before stepping up to the counter.
er_v06_c05_n001_03: Last night I was robbed. What little I had left is gone.
er_v06_c05_n001_04: The last of my money went on rent.
er_v06_c05_n001_05: The verdict came down. They found my mother guilty.
er_v06_c05_n001_06: I'll be trapped down here forever, and my mother will rot in prison.
er_v06_c05_n001_07: (She clutches the pendant, her voice shaking.)
er_v06_c05_n001_08: I can't believe I've sunk to asking this.
er_v06_c05_n001_09: But could you spare me some food? Anything edible, please.
er_v06_c05_n002_01: The shopkeeper pushes nutrifruit and dried rations toward her.
er_v06_c05_n002_03: She puts away the rations and nutrifruit, steps back, bows slightly, and only then turns to leave.
er_v06_c05_n003_01: He doesn't touch the bag on the counter.
er_v06_c05_n003_02: How much clearer do I have to be? My things were stolen, my money is gone, and the verdict is in. I am finished. Finished!
er_v06_c05_n004_01: The shopkeeper asks a few questions. She repeats what happened to her belongings.
er_v06_c05_n004_03: She folds the empty cloth bag and tucks it back into her jacket.
er_v06_c05_n005_01: (You can give her food, or money.)
er_v06_c18_b002_01: I brought some goods. This time I'm really here to sell.
er_v06_c18_b002_02: My mother gets up earlier than I do now. Two days ago I woke up and found her sitting there repairing an old tray.
er_v06_c18_b002_03: She says if her hands aren't doing something, she starts thinking about what happened in there.
er_v06_c18_b002_04: I handed her the tools and sat with her for a while.
er_v06_c18_b002_05: Nothing special. I just sat there for a while.
er_v06_c20_b001_01: I saw a batch of goods you might want. I didn't agree to anything for you.
er_v06_c20_b001_02: I asked where it came from, and what's broken. When the person arrives, you look for yourself.
er_v06_c20_b004_01: My mother says my tone when bargaining sounds more and more like yours.
er_v06_c20_b004_02: She says at least now I know what I'm talking about.
er_v06_c20_b004_03: I said the teacher is average. The student is the smart one.
er_v06_c20_b005_01: Isn't a clever girlfriend like me enough?
er_v06_c20_b005_02: You didn't argue with me this time. That counts as progress.
er_v06_c20_b006_01: Teach the new ones to tell a rusted connector from a good one first.
er_v06_c22_b001_01: My mother found a place willing to let her help organise equipment. Not her old farm, but she wants to go.
er_v06_c22_b001_02: I'll help out for a few days first. I found steadier work too, so I won't have to rely on scavenging.
er_v06_c22_b002_01: Someone from the research side came to ask if we'd help organise the records my mother left behind.
er_v06_c22_b002_02: Some of the work is up there. It needs a separate work permit. It's not a return to our old life, and the case isn't closed.
er_v06_c22_b002_03: My mother wants to keep doing research. I want to understand the parts I couldn't follow.
er_v06_c22_b003_01: Of course I'm going. I didn't come here today to ask for your permission.
er_v06_c22_b003_02: I came to work out the schedule with you.
er_v06_c22_b004_01: I want to keep working, and I want to keep seeing you.
er_v06_c22_b004_02: I'm not planning to drop the work, and I'm not planning to drop you.
er_v06_c22_b004_03: Now I choose for myself. Don't start deciding 'what's good for me' again.
er_v06_c22_b004_04: Say something when you're busy. Stop saying the shop can't spare you and then skipping proper meals.
er_v06_c22_b006_01: I might not come as often in the future. But we can still help each other with business.
er_v06_c22_b006_02: If you need anything, don't forget to come ask me.
er_v06_c22_b007_01: That time you asked the price, I didn't sell it. Do you remember?
er_v06_c22_b007_02: I told my mother I wanted to give it to you. She said it's mine, so I decide.
er_v06_c22_b007_03: It's not for sale. You'd better have learned the difference by now.
er_v06_c22_b008_01: Take it. Don't put it out with the stock. I'm not that generous.
er_v06_c22_b009_01: Fine, I'll wear it myself. You'll see it anyway.
er_v06_c22_b010_01: I originally wanted to give you that locket. In the end, I sold it to make up the money.
er_v06_c22_b010_02: You don't need to find something else to replace it. I just wanted you to know I thought about it.
er_v06_c23_b001_02: My mother's fine, and I still have my job.
er_v06_c23_b001_03: You'll have to get used to it. I don't only show up when something's wrong.
er_v06_c23_b002_01: My mother keeps telling me to bring an extra portion of food.
er_v06_c23_b002_03: The room's small, so we count every credit. Mother still has nightmares.
er_v06_c23_b002_04: When she wakes up, I'm right there.
er_v06_c23_b003_01: The first time I came here, I said this shop wasn't much. It still has plenty that needs fixing.
er_v06_c23_b003_02: Don't think that because I like you, I like the broken lights too. My temper doesn't disappear just because I'm in love.
er_v06_c23_b003_03: Let me stay a while today. If a customer comes, do your business.
er_v06_c23_b003_04: If no one comes, talk to me.
er_v06_c23_b003_05: Just don't start with 'how much more do you need?'
er_v06_c23_b004_01: Come to me if you need something. Or if you don't.
